question.problem:
Let $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ be a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- If $\text{Ker}(T)={[x,y,z]^{T}\,:\,y=z=0}$ then $\text{rank}(T)=2$
- If $Tx=[1,0,0]^{T}$ has more than one solution, then $\text{nullity}(T)=0$
- If $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$, then $T$ is invertible
question.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{3}$ into ${R}^{3},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=3 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)={0} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=3.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Since $y=z=0,$ any vector from $\text{Ker}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=x{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}.$ Therefore, $\text{nullity}(T)=1.$ Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T) & =3-\text{nullity}(T) \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since $Tx=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ has more than one solution, there are ${u}_{1},{u}_{2}\in {R}^{3}$ such that  ${u}_{1}\ne {u}_{2}$ and 

$$
T({u}_{1})=T({u}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

This means, $T$ is not a bijection and according to the invertible matrix theorem, $\text{nullity}(T)\ne 0.$

- Statement III is false. Notice that $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}.$ Therefore, $\text{nullity}(T)=1.$ So, $T$ is not a bijection or, which is the same, $T$ is not invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
